```lean
Std.Tactic.Lint.checkUnivs : Std.Tactic.Lint.Linter
```
***
A linter for checking that there are no bad `max u v` universe levels.
Checks whether all universe levels `u` in the type of `d` are "good".
This means that `u` either occurs in a `level` of `d` by itself, or (recursively)
with only other good levels.
When this fails, usually this means that there is a level `max u v`, where neither `u` nor `v`
occur by themselves in a level. It is ok if *one* of `u` or `v` never occurs alone. For example,
`(α : Type u) (β : Type (max u v))` is a occasionally useful method of saying that `β` lives in
a higher universe level than `α`.

***
*import Batteries.Tactic.Lint.Misc*

```lean
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.whiskerLeft_comp.{w, v, u} {B : Type u} [self : Bicategory B] {a b c : B} (f : a ⟶ b)
```

```lean
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.id_whiskerLeft.{w, v, u} {B : Type u} [self : Bicategory B] {a b : B} {f g : a ⟶ b}
  (η : f ⟶ g) : Bicategory.whiskerLeft (𝟙 a) η = (Bicategory.leftUnitor f).hom ≫ η ≫ (Bicategory.leftUnitor g).inv
```

```lean
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.comp_whiskerLeft.{w, v, u} {B : Type u} [self : Bicategory B] {a b c d : B} (f : a ⟶ b)
  (g : b ⟶ c) {h h' : c ⟶ d} (η : h ⟶ h') :
  Bicategory.whiskerLeft (f ≫ g) η =
    (Bicategory.associator f g h).hom ≫
      Bicategory.whiskerLeft f (Bicategory.whiskerLeft g η) ≫ (Bicategory.associator f g h').inv
```

```lean
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.whiskerRight_id.{w, v, u} {B : Type u} [self : Bicategory B] {a b : B} {f g : a ⟶ b}
```

```lean
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.whiskerRight_comp.{w, v, u} {B : Type u} [self : Bicategory B] {a b c d : B} {f f' : a ⟶ b}
  (η : f ⟶ f') (g : b ⟶ c) (h : c ⟶ d) :
  Bicategory.whiskerRight η (g ≫ h) =
    (Bicategory.associator f g h).inv ≫
      Bicategory.whiskerRight (Bicategory.whiskerRight η g) h ≫ (Bicategory.associator f' g h).hom
```

```lean
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.whisker_assoc.{w, v, u} {B : Type u} [self : Bicategory B] {a b c d : B} (f : a ⟶ b)
  {g g' : b ⟶ c} (η : g ⟶ g') (h : c ⟶ d) :
  Bicategory.whiskerRight (Bicategory.whiskerLeft f η) h =
    (Bicategory.associator f g h).hom ≫
      Bicategory.whiskerLeft f (Bicategory.whiskerRight η h) ≫ (Bicategory.associator f g' h).inv
```

```lean
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.whisker_exchange.{w, v, u} {B : Type u} [self : Bicategory B] {a b c : B} {f g : a ⟶ b}
  {h i : b ⟶ c} (η : f ⟶ g) (θ : h ⟶ i) :
  Bicategory.whiskerLeft f θ ≫ Bicategory.whiskerRight η i = Bicategory.whiskerRight η h ≫ Bicategory.whiskerLeft g θ
```

```lean
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.pentagon.{w, v, u} {B : Type u} [self : Bicategory B] {a b c d e : B} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c)
  (h : c ⟶ d) (i : d ⟶ e) :
  Bicategory.whiskerRight (Bicategory.associator f g h).hom i ≫
      (Bicategory.associator f (g ≫ h) i).hom ≫ Bicategory.whiskerLeft f (Bicategory.associator g h i).hom =
    (Bicategory.associator (f ≫ g) h i).hom ≫ (Bicategory.associator f g (h ≫ i)).hom
```

```lean
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.triangle.{w, v, u} {B : Type u} [self : Bicategory B] {a b c : B} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c) :
  (Bicategory.associator f (𝟙 b) g).hom ≫ Bicategory.whiskerLeft f (Bicategory.leftUnitor g).hom =
    Bicategory.whiskerRight (Bicategory.rightUnitor f).hom g
```

***
`term` is the builtin syntax category for terms. A term denotes an expression

```lean
ite.{u} {α : Sort u} (c : Prop) [h : Decidable c] (t e : α) : α
```
***
`if c then t else e` is notation for `ite c t e`, "if-then-else", which decides to
return `t` or `e` depending on whether `c` is true or false. The explicit argument
`c : Prop` does not have any actual computational content, but there is an additional
`[Decidable c]` argument synthesized by typeclass inference which actually
determines how to evaluate `c` to true or false. Write `if h : c then t else e`
instead for a "dependent if-then-else" `dite`, which allows `t`/`e` to use the fact
that `c` is true/false.
